items: Reporter · Anonymous [no authorization to use the name]

body.text: Reporter: once I od'd before the half-life had ended. It was a rather magical experience. Maybe only to me.

Reporter: the od itself was a bit uncomfortable — tachycardia, sweating and so on. But when I woke the next day: tinnitus, and my five senses felt expanded, extended. And I was happy all day, like a sound person, and it even carried into the next day.
Reporter: on the third day, when I od'd, I even had a feeling — ah, this is probably enough! And it did work. A slightly magical experience for me; sharing it with you.
Reporter: Teacher Pochi, actually when I od'd the first time, I felt I must have touched something similar as a child. But it doesn't matter; it just left me with a deep memory.

Reporter: what I wanted to tell you is that my drug resistance is a bit strange. And my od experiences. If you think it's okay, when you're in the mood, I'll come and write a little (probably while o-ing).
Reporter: today while taking dextro I took two levodopa... an indescribable feeling. An absolute pile of shit. God, the effects last forever.

Reporter: maybe I'm naturally sensitive, or maybe there's something wrong with my brain. When I feel something like 'surprise' now, I can very clearly feel a 'warm current' rushing up from below. That feeling, from love or something close to it, has happened three times in a short time, and it's different from anything any od drug has given me.
Reporter: but it could also be because of my unusual resistance to dissociation. I almost never dissociate; that 'light, floating' feeling rarely happens to me, even after taking large amounts.

Reporter: I'm conscious, my head is clear, I know what I'm doing, and my thinking is a little diffuse. Vision changes slightly, like the feel of the phone screen. But this probably isn't dissociation.
Reporter: I always feel I'm awake, and the drug in my head turns into waves of slight numbness, spreading or fading in my mind.

This is a 'counterexample': the reporter almost never dissociates, yet reports something like the afterglow. It supports 'the afterglow has more than one path', and it also reminds us not to reduce the afterglow to a single receptor.
The original text contained specific doses; they have been blacked out.
